faq.q: What is the origin of Bakhtawar?
faq.a: Bakhtawar is associated with Persian. Persian bakhtāwar ('fortunate'), from bakht ('fortune') and āwar ('bringing'). The source record classified it as Arabic, which is incorrect.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Bakhtawar can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Bakhtawar, bakhtawar. Script forms are بخت آور, بخت‌آور, बख़्तावर.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
